title: Charm City Kings — HBO Max AR Face Filters
subtitle: XR · Social · Campaign
heroImageAlt: They call me Holy Savage — Charm City Kings AR face filter frame

overview.label: Story
overview.heading: Overview
overview.body: A social AR campaign for HBO Max's first exclusive movie, Charm City Kings — Instagram face filters and a character name generator that let fans claim a Baltimore street name of their own.

problem.label: Problem
problem.heading: Why this needed to exist
problem.body: Charm City Kings arrived on HBO Max with no theatrical release, so awareness had to be won in feeds rather than lobbies. The campaign needed shareable, participatory content that put the movie's world — Baltimore dirt-bike culture, its nicknames and swagger — directly into fans' own faces.

approach.label: Approach
approach.heading: How the work got done
approach.body: Designed a set of 'They call me…' Instagram filters: a polaroid-style frame that dots the viewer's face camera and stamps a random street name — Mouse, Blax, Nicki, Holy Savage — over the shot, branded with the film's neon logo. Worked alongside the campaign build-out of social media assets to carry a consistent visual language from filters to feed.

outcomes.label: Outcomes
outcomes.heading: What changed once it shipped
outcomes.body: Launched as part of the movie's digital marketing push for its HBO Max premiere — fans shared their filter selfies with their new nicknames, turning every post into organic promotion for the October 8 release.

credits.label: Credits
credits.heading: One last thing
credits.body: Built for HBO Max — the Charm City Kings Instagram filters and name generator that shipped with the streaming premiere campaign.
